$comment: R7-05 requirement 5: a machine-readable finding -> CRITERION -> test-node matrix. Round 6's gate asserted only that a cited file EXISTS and mentions the finding — so a finding could read remediated while any individual acceptance criterion went unexercised, which is how R5-02's `[v1]` criterion was written down and never run. Each criterion here names a COLLECTED pytest node, checked against the actual collection rather than against the filesystem.

$proves: R8-06 requirement 5. A criterion whose value is an object declares WHAT EXTERNAL STATE its node asserts, so the release gate can report it rather than reporting only that a node was collected. The round-7 criteria keep the bare-string form: they were written before this field existed, and the three the review named as shallow — the SE pre-seal criterion, the invitation full-flow test and the shared-RdpId scan — were repointed at behavioural nodes in R8-01, R8-04 and R8-05 rather than annotated. Every criterion added from round 8 onward MUST carry `proves`, and no criterion of any round may name a source-inspection test.
$paired_with: R8-06: a criterion whose node inspects SOURCE may stand only when it names the behavioural node that would fail on the defect, and that node is itself in this matrix. Structural evidence is sometimes the only possible evidence — 'no branch selects behaviour by rule id' cannot be shown by running anything — but it may never be the ONLY evidence, which is how two source-order assertions came to stand for R7-01's output gate.
